sources.entry: pyinfra - Turns Python code into shell commands and runs them on your servers.

summary.one_liner: pyinfra is a Python-based automation tool that runs shell commands and declarative operations on SSH servers, the local machine, and Docker containers without installing agents.
summary.what_it_does: pyinfra turns Python code into shell commands and executes them on target hosts. It supports ad-hoc command execution via an exec operation and declarative operations (for example apt.packages) that describe desired state. Targets include SSH servers, the local machine, and Docker containers, and the README mentions connectors for Terraform and Vagrant as well. Operations are idempotent, which the README says enables diffs and dry runs before changes are made. Hosts can be defined in an inventory Python file and combined with deploy scripts on the command line. The README states it is agentless and can scale from one server to thousands.
use_cases: run ad-hoc commands across many hosts
manage Docker containers as deployment targets
install and maintain apt packages on servers
write infrastructure deployment scripts in Python
preview configuration changes with dry runs
notable: Agentless execution over SSH, local, and Docker targets
Operations are idempotent and support diffs and dry runs
Hosts and logic written in Python instead of YAML, usable with the full Python package ecosystem
caveats: The README does not state a license
Operations require shell access to the target hosts
